body_markdown:
If you asked Toyota to design[a Hot Wheels car](https://www.hagerty.com/media/news/this-excellent-el-camino-is-now-a-hot-wheels-legend/) , it would probably look a lot like this. Unveiled in Thailand, the Toyota Hilux Hyper Z Concept is a pickup with extensive modifications that wouldn’t look out of place on[a track-focused Italian supercar](https://www.hagerty.com/media/news/ferrari-296-challenge-stradale-and-challenge-evo-ditch-their-hybrid-systems-gain-speed/) .


Toyota’s Thai division developed the Hilux Hyper Z Concept with the help of Toyota’s Australian division. The partnership makes sense: Thailand is one of the countries that builds the Hilux for global markets, and Australians buy a lot of them—the truck held the third spot on the list of Australia’s best-selling car in 2025. The new concept has no interest in exploring the Outback, though.


Riding on 22-inch wheels, the Hyper Z stretches about 211 inches long, 87 inches wide, and 60 inches tall. The headlights and the grille are carried over from the regular-production Hilux, but that’s about it. Toyota added a new-look front bumper with air vents, a vented hood, and flared wheel arches that make this truck look like[a 1980s Group B rally car](https://www.hagerty.com/media/lists/10-hero-cars-of-group-b-rallying/) . The rear end is arguably even more extreme with a huge wing and a massive diffuser, and Toyota lowered the ride height to within a few inches of the ground.

Inside, it looks like the concept is a blend of stock and aftermarket parts. We spot the regular truck’s air vents and infotainment system, but the driver faces a Sabelt three-spoke steering wheel and a digital instrument cluster while sitting on a racing seat.


What the Hyper Z is powered by is up in the air. Toyota hasn’t released technical details. It’s not too far-fetched to speculate that there are no technical details to speak of, and that the concept is simply a rolling display of design wildness without a drivetrain.


As of writing, nothing suggests that the Toyota Hilux Hyper Z Concept is headed to production anywhere in the world. It was created to encourage buyers to customize their truck using the brand’s line of genuine accessories, though you’ll need to venture deep into the aftermarket if you want to build a truck close to it.


You’re not entirely out of luck if you want a Toyota pickup with an extra dose of performance: Recent reports[claim](https://www.hagerty.com/media/news/toyota-tundra-trd-hammer-raptor-rival-report/) that a Tundra-based model aimed at[the Raptor](https://www.hagerty.com/media/car-profiles/jurassic-park-driving-every-raptor-to-celebrate-15-years-of-madness/) and[the TRX](https://www.hagerty.com/media/new-car-reviews/2027-ram-1500-trx-srt-first-drive-ameritruck/) is on its way.
